stem.en: Which outer boundary would allow a cell to survive most successfully?

text.en: A solid, impenetrable wall with no openings.

feedback.en: A completely sealed wall would also keep out food, water and oxygen. A living cell must exchange materials continuously with its surroundings.

text.en: Eliminating the outer membrane entirely to maximize nutrient intake.

feedback.en: Without a membrane, the contents of the cell would simply mix with the outside environment. The cell could no longer maintain the conditions needed for life.

text.en: A flexible, semi-permeable membrane that selectively allows materials to pass.

explanation.en: A selectively permeable membrane protects the cell while still allowing nutrients, water and wastes to move in and out. This balance is essential for life.
